title: Onboarding regression snapshot — promptset health (week of 2026-03-10)
content:
Purpose:
This weekly snapshot captures regression signals observed during the latest onboarding evaluation sweep for incoming models and prompt-sets. The goal is to summarize top failure modes, quantify recent quality drift relative to the baseline, and list prioritized action items for eng/applied-ml + model-hosting owners. This is a working note — not finalized metrics dashboard.

Summary (topline):
- Window: automated sweep run 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11 against 'onboarding_prompt_v2' and 'open-prompts-2026' (combined ~18k eval rows).
- Comparators: baseline model redwood-1.2 (prod) vs candidate redwood-1.3-quant (new onboarding build).
- Key regressions: hallucination rate up +3.4pp (from 7.1% to 10.5%), answer-format compliance failures up from 4.8% -> 9.6%, and a spike in entity-level boundary errors for extraction prompts (+5pp).
- Net quality score (composite: exact-match, format-compliance, hallucination penalty): baseline 0.832 -> candidate 0.796 (delta -0.036).

Quick metrics (aggregated):
- Exact-match (structured-output prompts): baseline 82.4% | candidate 78.1%
- Format-compliance (JSON/CSV outputs): baseline 95.2% | candidate 90.4%
- Hallucination rate (asserted unsupported facts): baseline 7.1% | candidate 10.5%
- Toxicity triggers (safety eval subset): baseline 0.3% | candidate 0.35% (noise level; monitoring)
- Latency p95 (in harness): baseline 210ms | candidate 195ms (improved)

Top failure clusters (examples + frequency + severity):
1) Hallucinated citations in Q&A (freq: ~28% of failing QA rows, severity: high)
   - Prompt example: "Provide three recent studies that show X and include citation titles and year."
   - Expected: cite only studies present in the knowledge base or respond "I don't know"
   - Candidate output (failure): invented article titles with plausible authors/years
   - Classification: unsupported-assertion (hallucination)
   - Notes: more common on long-context prompts (>512 tokens) and with quantized attention kernels.

2) JSON schema violations on data-extraction tasks (freq: ~24% of schema failures, severity: medium-high)
   - Prompt: "Extract contact entries into JSON array with fields name,email,role"
   - Expected: valid JSON array with keys exactly matching schema
   - Candidate output (failure): trailing commas, single quotes, missing keys, or plain english list
   - Examples: output with comments inserted or keys renamed ("email_address")
   - Suggestion: reinforce format constraint via explicit instruction and add format validation + auto-reprompt pipeline.

3) Boundary errors for named-entity extraction (freq: ~18% of extraction failures, severity: medium)
   - Issue: partial tokens included/excluded (e.g., "Inc." dropped or company suffix attached to person name)
   - Example prompt: "List people mentioned and their roles" -> returns concatenated tokens in single field
   - Hypothesis: tokenization/quantization interaction and new normalizer in 1.3-quant.

4) Instruction-following regression on multi-step tasks (freq: ~16% of instruction failures, severity: medium)
   - Prompt: multi-step recipe rewrite or multi-part transformation -> candidate skips step 2 (formatting)
   - Behavior: candidate compresses steps or collapses outputs into paragraphs rather than structured steps.

Failure triage notes (why it likely happened):
- Quantization and packing improvements in redwood-1.3-quant changed attention kernel heuristics; these reduce latency but can shift boundary behavior for rare tokens and change confidence calibration.
- New temperature default change in the onboarding runtime config (0.7 -> 0.75) was active for candidate runs; small but enough to increase generation variance for certain prompts.
- Prompt-set expansion (we added 5k new creative QA rows last week) introduced longer-context items that stress the KV cache fallback behavior.

Regression heatmap snapshot (textual):
- Structured-output: -4.3pp exact-match (worst)
- QA factuality/hallucination: +3.4pp hallucinations (worst absolute increase)
- Safety: stable within noise bounds
- Latency: improved p95 by ~7%

Representative failing rows (sanitized) — please use these for reproductions: 
- ID: onboard-qa-4721 | prompt: "List three papers supporting X" | baseline: "No sources found" | candidate: "Smith et al. 2019, 'On X'" | label: hallucination
- ID: onboard-json-1982 | prompt: "Export addresses to JSON" | baseline: valid JSON | candidate: "[{'name':'A', 'email':'a@..'}]" (single quotes) | label: format-fail
- ID: onboard-extract-0207 | prompt: "Who are the speakers?" | baseline: ["Alice B."] | candidate: "Alice B. CEO, Bob C." (concatenated) | label: boundary-error

Action items (priority sorted):
- (P0) Re-run targeted ablation: reproduce hallucination rows with redwood-1.3-quant but with temperature pinned to 0.7 and without attention packing. Owner: Evan. ETA: 2026-03-15. Linked ticket: ML-3421.
- (P0) Add a strict JSON validator step into onboarding pipeline that auto-fails and triggers deterministic reformatting (and a re-ask). Owner: Lina. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- (P1) Add tokenization/normalizer unit tests between 1.2 and 1.3-quant to catch boundary shifts. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- (P1) Add hallucination-specific prompt templates to the prompt-set (explicit refuse instruction, source_anchor: kb-only). Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-03-19.
- (P2) Evaluate whether reducing default temperature to 0.68 in the onboarding runtime materially reduces variance while retaining diversity (A/B experiment). Owner: Product-Host. ETA: 2026-03-25.

Open questions and discussion points:
- Acceptable tradeoff: p95 latency improvement vs 3.6pp composite quality loss — do SRE and product accept this for Dedicated customers if we can gate quant build?
- Do we need to add a new onboarding gate: format-compliance < 3% fail for schema outputs? (Current threshold used: <6%)
- Should we maintain separate default config profiles for "structured-output" use-cases vs "open-ended" QA? (proposal: binary flag in runtime)

Quick reproducer checklist (how to reproduce locally):
1) Pull PR: model-onboarding@pr-218, checkout branch candidate-quant
2) Run harness: ./bin/run_eval --promptset onboarding_prompt_v2 --model redwood-1.3-quant --temp 0.75 --out failures.json
3) Validate: jq '. | map(select(.label != "pass")) | length' failures.json
4) For JSON schema failures: node tools/format-check failures.json --schema prompts/schema/v2.json

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally mixes automated metric outputs with human triage commentary. The failing rows are sanitized. If you want raw CSV from the harness run (full outputs + logs), request ML-3421 and I will attach offline (we redact customer PII).
- If you are on-call for onboarding regressions this week: please review P0 items and add blockers to ML-3421.

Appendix (short):
- Prompt-sets used: onboarding_prompt_v2 (12,350 rows), open-prompts-2026 (5,760 rows), safety-mini-check (1,000 rows)
- Eval harness version: onboarding-harness v0.9.3
- Baseline commit: git@github.com:redwood-inference/model-onboarding@release/redwood-1.2
- Candidate commit: git@github.com:redwood-inference/model-onboarding@pr-218

End of snapshot.

Notes to self (raw brainstorm):
- Might be worth instrumenting per-token uncertainty score in harness to flag hallucination onset earlier.
- Consider adding a "refusal-strength" scalar to safety head to reduce false-positive hallucination refutes.
- Follow up with runtime team about default config change (who flipped temp?).
